synopsis: NHTSA opened Preliminary Evaluation PE22-003 on 21 February 2022 after 278 complaints alleging inadvertent Honda Collision Mitigation Braking System activation, including 171 CR-V complaints and 107 Accord complaints [f1483, f15760]. The glossary adds that six complaints alleged a collision and some reported large speed changes despite nothing obstructing the vehicle’s path [f15760]. In April 2024, NHTSA upgraded the case to Engineering Analysis EA24-002, covering 2,997,604 vehicles across 2018–2022 Accord and 2017–2022 CR-V models, including hybrids; the glossary reports 1,294 complaints at that stage [f1485, f15761]. The skeptic’s review reiterates the engineering analysis’s date, false-braking focus and combined vehicle count, but the supplied facts give neither a CR-V-specific exposure count nor a final investigation outcome [f10422, f1485, f15761].
